facts.statement: The genus Clidastes was described by Edward Drinker Cope in 1868.
facts.quote: authority: Cope, 1868

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Clidastes is Clidastes propython.
facts.quote: type_species: Clidastes propython

facts.statement: Fossils of Clidastes date from the Coniacian to the Campanian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous, Coniacian-Campanian,

facts.statement: The name Clidastes means "locked vertebrae", derived from the Greek word for key.
facts.quote: Clidastes means "locked vertebrae", which originates from the Greek noun κλειδί, or kleid meaning key

facts.statement: The name refers to vertebral processes that interlock to provide stability and strength while swimming.
facts.quote: This refers to how the vertebral processes allow the proximal heads of the vertebrae to interlock for stability and strength during swimming.

facts.statement: Clidastes was likely an agile swimmer that hunted cephalopods, fish, and small vertebrates in shallow waters.
facts.quote: It was likely an agile swimmer that preyed upon cephalopods, fish and other small vertebrates in shallow water.

facts.statement: Isotopic analysis of teeth suggests Clidastes may have occasionally entered freshwater, similar to modern sea snakes.
facts.quote: Isotopic analysis on teeth specimens has suggested that this genus and Platecarpus may have entered freshwater occasionally, just like modern sea snakes.

facts.statement: The first specimens of Clidastes propython were discovered by E. D. Cope in 1869 in the Mooreville Chalk of Lowndes County, Alabama.
facts.quote: E. D. Cope discovered the first specimens of Clidastes propython in 1869 from the Mooreville Chalk in Lowndes County, Alabama.

facts.statement: The initial specimens found were a juvenile, representing one of the best-preserved and most complete mosasaurs from Alabama.
facts.quote: The remains unearthed were that of a juvenile but are one of the best preserved and most complete mosasaurs collected from the state

facts.statement: Additional remains of Clidastes were found in Kansas by Charles H. Sternberg and his son in 1918.
facts.quote: In 1918, Charles H. Sternberg and his son found additional remains of Clidastes in Kansas.

facts.statement: Specimens found in Kansas revealed humeri and femora with round heads, a feature similar to mammals.
facts.quote: They were surprised to see that it had humeri and femora with round heads, similar to that of mammals.

facts.statement: Good preservation allowed Sternberg to note that chevrons were ankylosed to the center of the vertebrae, a trait not seen in other mosasaurs.
facts.quote: Due to good preservation of the caudals, Sternberg noted that the chevrons along the vertebrae were ankylosed to the center, which is not observed in other mosasaurs.

facts.statement: Clidastes had a delicate, slim form with expanded neural spines and chevrons near the tail tip, enabling it to chase fast prey.
facts.quote: It possessed a delicate and slim form with an expansion of the neural spines and chevrons near the tip of the tail and this enabled it to chase down the fastest of prey.

facts.statement: Clidastes is firmly placed in the subfamily Mosasaurinae due to its dental and vertebral morphology being closer to Mosasaurus than any other mosasaur.
facts.quote: The dental and vertebral morphology of Clidastes is closer to that of Mosasaurus than to any other mosasaur, firmly placing it within the subfamily Mosasaurinae.

facts.statement: Clidastes is often recovered as a basal mosasaurine and the most basal hydropedal mosasaurine genus, more derived than Dallasaurus but less derived than Prognathodon or Globidens.
facts.quote: Clidastes is most frequently recovered as one of the most basal mosasaurines, and the most basal hydropedal mosasaurine genus, being more derived than the plesiopedal Dallasaurus but less derived than later genera like Prognathodon or Globidens.

facts.statement: Currently, only one species, C. propython, is considered valid within the genus Clidastes.
facts.quote: There is only one named species of Clidastes that is valid, C. propython.

facts.statement: C. iguanavus was the original type species, but C. propython was designated the new type species by the ICZN in 1993 based on diagnostic remains.
facts.quote: Clidastes iguanavus Cope, 1868 was the original type species, but the ICZN was petitioned to make C. propython the new type species by virtue of that species being based on diagnostic remains, which it did vis-à-vis Opinion 1750 (1993).

facts.statement: Mosasaur teeth, including those of Clidastes, typically have a pointed, curved crown sitting on a bony pedicel.
facts.quote: Mosasaur teeth are of rather uniform morphology (with a few exceptions, such as in Globidens) with a pointed and curved tooth crown that sits on a pedicel composed of bone.

facts.statement: The marginal tooth rows in Clidastes are located on the premaxilla, maxilla, and dentary.
facts.quote: The marginal tooth rows in mosasauroids like Clidastes are found on the premaxilla, maxilla and the dentary.

facts.statement: The genus Clidastes was named by Cope in 1868.
facts.quote: genus: Clidastes Cope, 1868

facts.statement: Clidastes propython was designated the type species of the genus by Cope in 1869.
facts.quote: subdivision: C. propython Cope, 1869 (tipo)

facts.statement: Clidastes lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Clidastes es un género de mosasáuridos que vivieron en el Cretácico superior en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Clidastes had a narrow head and slender body, giving it a very hydrodynamic shape.
facts.quote: Tenían una cabeza estrecha y un cuerpo esbelto, lo que le confería una forma muy hidrodinámica.

facts.statement: They are not considered very agile because their flippers were not fully webbed.
facts.quote: No se les considera muy hábiles, ya que sus aletas no estaban totalmente palmeadas.

facts.statement: They possessed nerve branches extending to the tip of the tail, which would allow them to beat the water to move at high speeds.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, poseían ramificaciones nerviosas que se extienden hasta la punta de la cola, lo que les permitiría batir el agua para moverse a grandes velocidades.

facts.statement: The genus existed from the Turonian to the Maastrichtian, between 93.9 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Maastrichtian (93.9 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Clidastes liodontus was described from the Smoky Hill Chalk Member of the Niobrara Formation in Kansas.
facts.quote: Clidastes liodontus was described from the late Coniacian to early Campanian Smoky Hill Chalk Member of the Niobrara Formation in Kansas.

facts.statement: Lively (2019) declared C. liodontus a nomen dubium and recommended restricting the genus to C. propython.
facts.quote: Lively (2019) declared Clidastes liodontus a nomen dubium, while taking note of the nomen nudum status of "moorevillensis", recommending that Clidastes be restricted to C. propython.

facts.statement: C. propython was chosen by the ICZN to replace C. iguanavus as the type species because it is the best studied.
facts.quote: C. propython is the best studied species of the genus, and was for this reason chosen by the ICZN to replace C. iguanavus as the type species.

facts.statement: The species lived from the middle Santonian to the Middle to Late Campanian, coinciding with an extinction event that heavily affected Clidastes.
facts.quote: The earliest known occurrences of the species are middle Santonian in age and from the Niobrara Formation of Kansas, whilst the latest are Middle to Late Campanian in age, coinciding with a poorly understood middle Campanian intercontinental mosasaur extinction event, which seems to have heavily affected genera such as Clidastes.

facts.statement: The premaxillary suture of the maxilla was smoothly keeled and parallel to the longitudinal axis, with sixteen to eighteen teeth in the maxilla.
facts.quote: Premaxillary suture of maxilla smoothly keeled and paraIIels longitudinal axis of maxilla. Sixteen-18 teeth in maxilla.

facts.statement: C. iguanavus is the original type species of Clidastes but is poorly known compared to other species.
facts.quote: The Campanian C. iguanavus is the original type species of Clidastes and poorly known in comparison to C. propython and C. liodontus.

facts.statement: C. iguanavus can be differentiated by kidney-shaped central articulations and stout centrum proportions.
facts.quote: C. iguanavus can be differentiated in its central articulations, which are kidney-shaped in outline, with a stronger emargination dorsally for the spinal cord, and in the relatively stout proportions of the centrum.

facts.statement: Specimens have been referred to this genus from marine deposits in Sweden, Germany, Russia, Mexico, and Jordan.
facts.quote: Clidastes is currently found in marine deposits in the US. In past, however, specimens were referred to this genus from Sweden, Germany, Russia, Mexico, and the Maastrichtian of Jordan.

facts.statement: Lively (2019) questioned the referral of remains from outside the US to Clidastes due to their fragmentary nature.
facts.quote: However, Lively (2019) questioned the referral of these remains to Clidastes due to their fragmentary nature and lack of apomorphies placing them in the genus to the exclusion of other mosasaurs.
